clue.text: Be thrifty with seafood that's cold instead of hot

indicators.note: the tap letters swap: C for cold takes the place of H for hot in the seafood word

parts.note: a shrimp is a small edible crustacean, a kind of seafood

explanation.surface: Advice to economise by eating cold prawns rather than a hot dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cold instead of hot' swaps the H of SHRIMP for a C, the abbreviations found on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise hard, cutting spending to the bone, which is being thrifty.

clue.text: Popular fellow by window on plane trip

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a light is a window pane or opening that lets light in

explanation.surface: A well-liked man gets the window seat on his flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just places the pieces side by side; LIGHT as a window pane is an older sense still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: In-flight describes what happens aboard an aircraft during a journey, such as catering or films.

clue.text: One who's bound to turn the raw pickle — it's not briny

indicators.note: to be in a pickle is to be in a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: a serf was bound to the land he worked, an unfree labourer
taken as written, the letters of these two words join the anagram

explanation.surface: A captive slave is made to pickle raw food, though without salt.
explanation.walkthrough: SERF plus THE RAW is ten letters that 'pickle' rearranges; 'to turn' reads as a link, the serf being made to take a turn at the job.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh water lacks salt, so it is the opposite of briny sea water.

clue.text: Pleased with little flower

definitions.meaning: a short informal name for the gladiolus, a garden flower with tall spikes of blooms

explanation.definitionFit: Glad means happy, and is also the familiar clipped name of the gladiolus bloom.

clue.text: Shrewd boss yearned to provide cover

indicators.note: the yearning word wraps itself round the other, covering it on both sides

parts.note: longed means yearned or desired strongly
the head is the boss or chief of an organisation

explanation.surface: A clever manager longed to shield his staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to provide cover' means the yearning word wraps round the boss, so the whole splits as LONG-HEAD-ED with the boss sitting in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-headed is a dated word for far-sighted and canny, i.e. sagacious or shrewd.

clue.text: Dodgy dealer setting up big shots

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: VIPs are very important persons, big shots

explanation.surface: A shady trader is arranging deals with important people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting up' turns VIPS upwards in this down entry. A SPIV is British slang for a flashy petty black-marketeer.
explanation.definitionFit: A spiv is a smartly dressed man living by shady trading, a crooked dealer.

clue.text: Fish seen after seafront walk

indicators.note: the fishing word comes after the first piece

parts.note: the front of the word sea is its first letter, S
to troll is to fish by trailing a baited line behind a boat

explanation.surface: Someone spots a fish after a walk along the promenade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seafront' is read as the front of 'sea'; 'seen' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroll is a leisurely walk or saunter.

clue.text: Do without moving metal

parts.note: a cast holds a broken limb rigid so it cannot move, so cast stands for kept immobile
to iron is to do the laundry, pressing clothes

explanation.surface: An instruction to manage without shifting some metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: IRON for 'Do' (as in doing the shirts) and CAST for 'without moving'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cast iron is an iron alloy shaped in a mould, a familiar engineering metal.

clue.text: Noted female officer in funny cartoon

indicators.note: the officer's letters go inside the rearranged ones
something funny is odd, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

explanation.surface: A well-known woman officer appears in a comic strip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' looks like 'famous' but means singing notes. 'funny' rearranges the comic strip's letters to CONTRAO, and 'in' sets the officer inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A contralto is the lowest female singing voice, so a female singer of notes.

clue.text: World Heritage site, one favoured by academy

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, someone favoured
RA is the Royal Academy of Arts in London

explanation.surface: A famous protected site is a favourite of the academy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' just puts the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra, the rock-cut city in Jordan, is listed by UNESCO as a heritage location.

clue.text: Badly sullied, badly treated

indicators.note: done badly, the letters are put in a poor order

explanation.surface: Something dirtied and mistreated.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'Badly' rearranges SULLIED; the second belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-used means mistreated or abused by others.

clue.text: Respond to appeal and run short

definitions.meaning: in cricket an umpire answers a fielder's appeal by declaring the batter dismissed
supplies run out or become exhausted

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the fielders appeal ('Howzat?') and the umpire may raise a finger to dismiss the batter.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket umpire upholding an appeal dismisses the batter; supplies that are exhausted also fail.

clue.text: Girl to hold at fixed level

definitions.meaning: A pet form of the woman's name Margaret
to fix prices or rates so they stay at one value

explanation.definitionFit: Peg is a short girl's name, and pegging a currency fixes its value.

clue.text: Sort of work for actor-will he play?

indicators.note: to play with something is to toy with it, so the letters move about

explanation.surface: Asking whether a performer will take the part.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen is ignored: 'play' rearranges the eleven letters of ACTOR WILL HE.
explanation.definitionFit: White-collar work is office or clerical work, as opposed to manual labour.

clue.text: Polar mines, terribly cold

indicators.note: done terribly, the letters end up jumbled

explanation.surface: Arctic mines are bitterly chilly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polar' and 'cold' make a frosty picture, but cold here is unfriendly, not chilly.
explanation.definitionFit: Impersonal behaviour is detached and lacking warmth, a cold manner.

clue.text: Ring with faint aroma and with varied hues

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
pale means faint or weak in colour
a scent is an aroma or smell

explanation.surface: A ring giving off a faint perfume and shimmering in many colours.
explanation.walkthrough: Both 'with's are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Opalescent describes a milky iridescence like opal, showing shifting colours.

clue.text: First bit of toast covered with butter is nobbled

indicators.note: the opening letter is wrapped by the second piece

parts.note: a goat butts with its head, so it is a butter

indicators.note: the first bit of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A slice of toast spread with butter has been tampered with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is one that butts, a GOAT, not the spread; 'covered with' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be got at is to be nobbled, i.e. bribed or tampered with improperly.

clue.text: Visit daughter and deteriorate

parts.note: to visit someone is to go to see them

explanation.surface: Calling on one's daughter and going downhill.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to seed is to decline in condition or looks, as plants do when they bolt.

clue.text: Cushion required for Father Ted's back

parts.note: Pa is a familiar word for father

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A priest named Ted needs a cushion for his sore back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'required for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is a soft cushion or wad of padding.

clue.text: Management having little time after short notice

indicators.note: the time piece comes after the notice piece

parts.note: ad is short for advertisement, a notice
min is short for minute, a small amount of time

explanation.surface: Bosses are given hardly any time after a brief warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short notice' looks like a hurry, but it is an ad, a notice cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: Admin is short for administration, the management of an organisation.

clue.text: Tongue is orange — and that's official!

definitions.meaning: a senior bureaucrat, from the old Chinese imperial civil service

explanation.definitionFit: Chinese language, small citrus fruit and high-ranking civil servant all share this name.

clue.text: Drag queen game? Capital sight!

parts.note: to tow is to drag or haul along
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: A drag queen invites everyone to a card game, a sight to see in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drag queen' looks like one phrase but must be split into two pieces. TOWER BRIDGE is the landmark bascule bridge over the Thames in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tower Bridge is one of London's famous landmarks, a tourist sight in the capital.

clue.text: Leaders of West Indian band providing work for electrician

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

parts.note: a ring is a band, such as a wedding band

explanation.surface: Caribbean bandleaders hire someone to fix the electrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians but is a ring; 'providing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Installing cables and circuits in a building is the electrician's job.

clue.text: Bradman retrospectively gives sign of assent

indicators.note: looking back, the word is read in reverse

parts.note: Sir Donald Bradman, the great Australian cricketer, known as the Don

explanation.surface: The great cricketer, looking back, signals agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: Don Bradman was the outstanding Australian batsman, universally called 'the Don'.
explanation.definitionFit: A nod of the head is a gesture of agreement.

clue.text: Presentable rendering of number in France

parts.note: de is French for of
cent is French for a hundred, a number

explanation.surface: A tidy translation of a French figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in France' marks both words as French; 'rendering' is a link, a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Decent means respectable or adequate, fit to be seen.

clue.text: After manoeuvres Osric gets the commander on the blower

indicators.note: after being moved about, the name has its letters rearranged

parts.note: CO is commanding officer

explanation.surface: Following exercises, Osric phones his commanding officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the blower' suggests the telephone; the blower is the wind itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The sirocco is a hot wind from North Africa, so a blower.

clue.text: There's something to be said for a sheath

definitions.meaning: an argument in favour, as in having a good one to make
a covering or holder, such as a pillowcase or knife sleeve

explanation.definitionFit: A case is an argument made for something, and also a covering or container.

clue.text: Old-fashioned roguish spies making a comeback

parts.note: arch means playfully mischievous or roguish

indicators.note: coming back, the word is read in the other direction

parts.note: the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: Dated cheeky secret agents return to the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Archaic means very old or antiquated, belonging to an earlier time.

clue.text: Legislation that is followed by Romans

definitions.meaning: in the New Testament the book of the Apostles' deeds comes just before Paul's letter to the Romans

explanation.definitionFit: Laws are passed as statutes, and the biblical book of the apostles precedes Romans.

clue.text: Sport not originating in an Irish county town

indicators.note: without its origin, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: tennis is a sport

explanation.surface: A sport not invented in an Irish town.
explanation.walkthrough: Ennis is the county town of County Clare in Ireland; 'in an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennis is the administrative centre of County Clare.

clue.text: On the hour it turns on word of command

parts.note: at ten is a time exactly on the hour

indicators.note: the little word turns round, reading backwards

parts.note: taken as written before turning
taken as written

explanation.surface: At the top of the hour, a soldier spins round at the order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turns' reverses the little word 'it', which sits between the time and 'on'; ten o'clock is exactly on the hour.
explanation.definitionFit: A drill sergeant's order to stand straight is a command word.
